root.name: Tarrasch Defense: Dubov Tarrasch
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 c5 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. g3 Nf6 7. Bg2 cxd4 8. Nxd4 Bc5

overview: In this Prague Tarrasch Black develops 8...Bc5 attacking the knight on d4. Play turns on Black's isolated d5 pawn, active pieces and the bishop pair against White's blockade with Nb3 and the Bg2 pressure.

white_ideas.idea: Trade pieces to exploit the isolated pawn

black_ideas.idea: Use open lines for the bishops

typical_structures.structure: Isolated queen's pawn for Black on d5

character.notes: Active piece play with chances to attack, but not wildly tactical.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

structure.notes: Asymmetric structure with an IQP and open c-file, so semi-open.

character.reason: Active play for the IQP with real risk but no forced attack.

structure.reason: The asymmetric IQP structure and open c-file.

level.reason: Managing the IQP is a plan-based skill.

plans.reason: Black's isolated queen's pawn gives active pieces.
